options: Hides details so you can focus on what something does
check.explanation: Abstraction hides the how so you can work with the what. It does not make code faster, and functions are one of the main ways to build it.

check.prompt: Which is an example of abstraction?
options: Copying the same code into three places
Calling sort() without knowing which sorting algorithm it uses
check.explanation: You use sort() through its name and what it promises, and the algorithm inside stays hidden. The other two make code harder to understand.
check.hint: Look for the one where details are hidden behind a simple name.

check.prompt: Why is hiding the details useful?
options: The inside can change later without breaking the people who use it
It makes the program shorter in every case
It means nobody needs to test it
check.explanation: If callers only rely on what the function promises, you can improve the inside freely. Abstraction does not remove the need to test.
check.hint: What can you do to the inside if nobody depends on it?
